title: Pat Gelsinger:  "HBM is a hideous memory"
gist: Pat Gelsinger, Intel's former CEO, called HBM a 'hideous memory' with poor bit density plus shoreline-bandwidth, power and thermal limits, repeating a July 'lousy memory' remark; the post also notes Nanya reiterating DRAM shortages until 2028. This is a forum repost of a wccftech item quoting the a16z interview.

insights.claim: Pat Gelsinger says HBM is a poor memory architecture for AI because of terrible bit density, shoreline bandwidth limits, power and thermal issues, calling it merely the best option currently available.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Signals an opening for alternative memory architectures if HBM's constraints persist.
insights.quote: HBM is a hideous memory. That’s just the best one that we got.

insights.claim: Gelsinger argues DRAM does not tolerate heat and HBM concentrates everything in one spot, creating thermal problems for memory-compute AI workloads.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Thermal limits are a structural constraint on HBM stacking and a theme for cooling and packaging.
insights.quote: DRAM doesn’t like to be hot.

insights.claim: Gelsinger made a similar remark in July at the RAISE Summit, calling HBM a 'lousy' memory, so the criticism is consistent rather than a one-off.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Repeated public stance suggests a deliberate narrative, possibly tied to his current investing and advisory interests.
insights.locator: Do note that Pat Gelsinger echoed similar disparaging remarks

insights.claim: Nanya reiterated that DRAM shortages will last until 2028.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Prolonged DRAM tightness supports memory pricing and supplier earnings.
